meaning: The thing one stage of the loop hands to the next, such as a decoded frame, a simulation step, a training sample or an action, counted per second to compare machines.
A computer that sits beside the robot, where power is the scarce resource and nothing is billed by the hour.
A small program that loads a machine the way a real workload does without being that workload.
Units of work per second divided by watts drawn: how much work a machine does with a fixed amount of energy.
How an instance hour is bought: on demand, as spare capacity that AWS can take back, or as a reservation; each has its own price.
The AWS location an instance runs in; prices differ between Regions.
One GPU running for one hour.
The time between two commands to the motors: 33.3 ms when the arm is driven at 30 Hz.
Several future actions returned by one policy call, played while the next call computes.
The time within which half of all calls finish; it describes the typical call.
The time within which ninety-nine calls in every hundred finish; a robot's deadline is judged against it.
The Jetson's own command-line monitor of power and load.
NVIDIA's command-line tool that reports GPU status, including utilisation and power.
AWS's own Arm processors, offered as EC2 CPU instances.
